newsitem.title: UK: AUSTRALIA TOPS GLOOMY WEEK FOR BONDS - SALOMON.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA TOPS GLOOMY WEEK FOR BONDS - SALOMON.

text.p: Australian bonds made the best of a bad job last week, racking up the least losses of all major markets, according to the latest data from Salomon Brothers on Friday.
Australian paper lost 0.05 percent in local currency terms in the week to August 6, compared with losses of up to 1.02 percent in the case of worst performer Denmark.
The Salomon Brothers World Government Bond Index (WGBI) of 17 markets lost 0.56 percent in local currency terms in the latest week and 1.52 percent in dollar terms.
Currency woes in Europe and a stronger than expected July U.S. payrolls report took their toll on global bond markets.
Japan escaped relatively unscathed, showing a loss of 0.08 percent in yen terms and 0.62 percent in dollar terms.
Finland, Switzerland and Sweden were next in line with losses of 0.42 percent, 0.44 and 0.51 percent respectively.

But Italy was close at Denmark's heels in terms of poor performance, making a 1.0 percent loss on the week in lira terms and a whopping 3.57 percent loss in dollar terms -- the worst performing market in dollars.
France fared only marginally better, showing a 0.97 percent loss in francs and a 3.05 percent fall in dollars.

Germany managed a slightly better performance than most of its European neighbours, as the mark steadied on European crosses. It suffered a 0.57 percent loss in local currency terms, but a 2.52 percent decline in dollar terms.
Of the dollar bloc, U.S. T-bonds lost 0.61 percent and Canada lost 0.56 percent in Canadian dollars.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
